title: G1 C8 · Food Health and Safety

questions.q: A balanced diet keeps us healthy. State what a balanced diet contains.
choices: the right amounts of all nutrients
questions.explain: A balanced diet contains all the nutrients in the right amounts. It is not equal amounts of each nutrient, because we need more of some than others.

questions.q: Proteins are a nutrient in our food. State the function of proteins.
questions.explain: Proteins are needed for growth and for repairing damaged tissues. Carbohydrates are the main source of energy.

questions.q: Iron is a mineral salt. State the function of iron in the body.
questions.explain: Iron is needed to make red blood cells, which carry oxygen in the blood. Too little iron causes anaemia.

questions.q: Fruits are rich in vitamin C. State the function of vitamin C.
questions.explain: Vitamin C keeps the gums healthy and stops them from bleeding. A lack of vitamin C causes scurvy.

questions.q: Cod liver oil is rich in vitamin D. State the function of vitamin D.
questions.explain: Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium. Calcium is then used to build strong bones and teeth.

questions.q: Name the nutrient in vegetables that helps to prevent constipation.
questions.explain: Dietary fibre adds bulk to food so it moves easily through the gut. This helps to prevent constipation.

questions.q: Identify the food that is a good source of carbohydrates.
questions.explain: Rice is rich in starch, which is a carbohydrate. Fish and eggs are rich in protein, and butter is rich in fat.

questions.q: Identify the food that is a good source of protein.
questions.explain: Fish is rich in protein. Potatoes and bread are rich in carbohydrates, and cooking oil is fat.

questions.q: Chicken skin is greasy. Name the main nutrient in chicken skin.
questions.explain: Greasy foods are rich in fats. Chicken skin is mostly fat.

questions.q: Calcium builds strong bones and teeth. Identify a good source of calcium.
questions.explain: Milk is a good source of calcium. Oranges are rich in vitamin C, rice in carbohydrates and oil in fat.

questions.q: My Healthy Plate shows a healthy meal. State what fills half the plate.
questions.explain: On My Healthy Plate, half the plate is fruits and vegetables. A quarter is whole grains and a quarter is meat and other proteins.

questions.q: On My Healthy Plate, one quarter is whole grains. Name what fills the other quarter.
questions.explain: My Healthy Plate is half fruits and vegetables, a quarter whole grains, and a quarter meat and other proteins.

questions.q: A food label shows 200 Calories per serving. Calculate the Calories in 2 servings.
questions.explain: Each serving has 200 Calories. Two servings have 2 × 200 = 400 Calories.

questions.q: One serving of cereal has 5 g of protein. Calculate the protein in 4 servings.
questions.explain: Each serving has 5 g of protein. Four servings have 4 × 5 g = 20 g of protein.

questions.q: A cup of soup has 200 Calories. Calculate the number of cups that give 500 Calories.
questions.explain: Number of cups = 500 Calories ÷ 200 Calories per cup = 2.5 cups.

questions.q: A serving has 240 mg of sodium. Sodium Daily Value is 2400 mg. Calculate the %DV.
The fat Daily Value is 65 g. Calculate 10% of this mass.
%DV means percentage Daily Value. State the %DV that is considered high.
questions.explain: A %DV of 20% or more is high. A %DV of 5% or less is low.

questions.q: Identify the diet that can lead to high blood pressure.
questions.explain: A diet high in salt can lead to high blood pressure. Calcium, protein and fibre do not cause it.

questions.q: Fat can build up inside blood vessels. Name the disease this can lead to.
questions.explain: Fat that builds up inside blood vessels makes them narrower. The heart must then pump harder, which leads to high blood pressure.

questions.q: A diet is high in sugar. Name a disease it can lead to.
questions.explain: A diet high in sugar can lead to diabetes. In diabetes the body cannot control the amount of sugar in the blood.

questions.q: A diet lacks fibre and water. Name the problem it can lead to.
questions.explain: Fibre and water help food move easily through the gut. Without enough of them, the faeces become hard, which is constipation.

questions.q: In diabetes, a substance in the blood cannot be controlled. Name the substance.
questions.explain: In diabetes the body cannot control the amount of glucose, a sugar, in the blood.

questions.q: Name the food test used to detect starch.
questions.explain: The iodine test detects starch. The biuret test detects protein and the oil blot test detects oil.

questions.q: Biuret solution is blue. State its colour after it is added to protein.
questions.explain: Biuret solution turns from blue to violet when protein is present.

questions.q: Iodine solution on a food turns from brown to blue-black. Identify the nutrient present.
questions.explain: Iodine solution turns from brown to blue-black when starch is present.

questions.q: Biuret solution added to a food turns from blue to violet. Identify the nutrient present.
questions.explain: Biuret solution turns from blue to violet when protein is present.

questions.q: A food rubbed on paper leaves a translucent mark. Identify the nutrient present.
questions.explain: Oil leaves a translucent mark on paper that light can pass through. This is the oil blot test.

questions.q: Define microbes.
choices: tiny organisms we can easily see
tiny organisms too small to see
tiny organisms that are all harmful
tiny organisms that are all moulds
questions.explain: Microbes are living things too small to see with our eyes alone. Some are harmful, but many are useful.

questions.q: Eating food with harmful microbes can make us sick. Name this illness.
questions.explain: Food poisoning is an illness caused by eating food that contains harmful microbes or their poisons.

questions.q: Old bread has a fluffy green growth on it. Name this type of microbe.
questions.explain: A fluffy green or black growth on old bread is mould. Mould is a fungus.

questions.q: Pickling keeps food in vinegar. Explain how pickling preserves food.
questions.explain: Vinegar is an acid, so pickling lowers the pH of the food. Most microbes cannot grow in such acidic conditions.

questions.q: Dehydration means drying food. Explain how dehydration preserves food.
questions.explain: Microbes need water to grow. Drying the food lowers its water content, so microbes cannot grow.

questions.q: Bottling seals food in airtight bottles. Explain how bottling preserves food.
questions.explain: Sealing food in airtight bottles cuts off the supply of oxygen. Many microbes need oxygen to grow.

questions.q: Sterilisation heats food to a high temperature. Explain how sterilisation preserves food.
questions.explain: Sterilisation heats food to a high temperature. The heat kills the microbes in the food.

questions.q: Identify the preservation method that lowers the pH of food.
questions.explain: Pickling keeps food in vinegar, which is acidic. This lowers the pH of the food.

questions.q: Vitamins and mineral salts are added to food. Identify the type of food additive.
questions.explain: Vitamins and mineral salts are added to make food more nutritious. These additives are nutrient supplements.

questions.q: Food colourings are added to food. Identify the type of food additive.
questions.explain: Food colourings change how food looks. They are texture and appearance modifiers.

questions.q: Sulfur dioxide is a preservative. Predict an effect of eating too much of it.
questions.explain: Too much sulfur dioxide can cause allergic reactions in some people, such as breathing problems for people with asthma.
